report.source_text: The patient deferred treatment options during her hospital stay and was discharged in stable condition after receiving diuretics with the improvement of her lower extremity edema, shortness of breath, and orthopnea. Upon follow-up with the patient’s primary care provider, the patient endorsed continued improvement of her functional status while on maintenance diuretics. The patient decided against bulk resection of her tumor with the surgical team; however, she started targeted molecular therapy with imatinib 100 mg twice daily.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Spindle cell tumor suggestive of a GIST
clinician.trajectory_summary: An 89-year-old female presented with worsening lower extremity edema, dyspnea, orthopnea, early satiety, generalized abdominal pain, and weight loss. Physical exam revealed bilateral pitting edema and diffuse abdominal distention with tenderness. An abdominal CT scan showed a large 15x22x23 cm solid and cystic supracolic intraperitoneal mass with cystic necrosis and significant mass effect. An image-guided biopsy of the mass was performed, and histopathological analysis characterized the tissue as a spindle cell tumor suggestive of a GIST. The patient declined surgical resection, was treated with diuretics leading to symptomatic improvement, and later started targeted molecular therapy with imatinib. She was discharged in stable condition and showed functional improvement on follow-up.
